label: m5_policy
history_use: At each of her notes Duet looks at what she has just sung (the main note of each of the last 7 beats and the last bar), which notes this song has used so far, and a per-song memory of what she sang the last time the same situation came up earlier in this song; a small neural net turns that plus her current note into a score for each possible harmony note (will it agree with her AND fit the song's chord), and Duet picks the best-scoring note close to its previous one. History helps because the chord usually lasts across several notes, so recent notes tell Duet which chord is playing: with zero history the same net scores 0.628 vs 0.666 with full history (matched low doubling), and almost all of that gain comes from the last 4 beats (0.662).

ablation.reading: History length matters (0 beats -> -0.038), but only the last ~4 beats; the 3 feature groups are largely redundant: dropping recent notes (ctx) costs most (-0.008), dropping per-song memory -0.004, dropping the song histogram ~0. The other big lever is the doubling weight: allowing octave doubling up to ~24% lifts music 0.666 -> 0.714, so about half of the gain over v1 is echoing her in octaves where that is consonant and a chord tone, not better chord tracking.

what_failed: Doubling budget driven by Duet's own past doubling rate (v7, 0.692) was worse than a flat doubling weight (v5, 0.709); a bigger net/more rows (v8) gave +0.001; lower step costs (v12, v13) did not help. v9's max doubling is 0.237 (bach/folk), close to the 0.25 flag; m5_policy_v10 (0.701, max doubling 0.176) is the safe fallback. Limitations: DUET_HIST limits all feature groups (ctx, partial beat, previous note, histogram, memory, bar vectors) but the weights are retrained per N (cached by N); training rows are capped at 90k notes per dataset.
